svg.aria-label: One release-46 play decision, drawn from a live lead in room ADKY: seat 3 holds 3, 5, 7, 8, Q, A of clubs and the jack of diamonds; the S17 belief model gives each hidden card's holder probabilities (26.9 ms); 66 worlds are drawn, 2 rejected as history-illegal, 64 kept; 8 of 64 legal plays are admitted with their policy log-odds; the value head scores each candidate in each world and the mean picks the ace of clubs (1.799); the value step is 512 positions (values) in 4 forward calls (batches of 128). Exact endgame at 7 or fewer cards per hand, in five steps: the 64 belief worlds; play each candidate (on a lead the heuristic finishes trick 1); try each one with all hands face up to the round's end; average over the 64 worlds; pick the best average. On one world, the true deal, the J of diamonds and the ace of clubs both end with attackers on 45 (+1 level) and the 5, 8, ace of clubs with attackers on 80, a lost deal. Alpha-beta pruning and a transposition-table cache: 429,026 positions tried, 173,315 reused, 0.197 s. Mean J of diamonds 1.797 vs ace of clubs 1.719, so the J of diamonds plays, in 0.49 s.
svg.text: Live lead in room ADKY (release 46): seat 3, no trump, 7 cards per hand. 64 legal plays → 8 candidates → J♦ in 0.49 s.
ONE WORLD, STEP ③ (HERE: THE TRUE DEAL)
tie in this world; the 64-world average breaks it
Alpha-beta pruning + a transposition-table cache (429,026 positions tried, 173,315 reused, 0.197 s); on budget expiry the value-head pick stands.
mean J♦ 1.797 vs A♣ 1.719 → J♦ (value units: +1 level = 1.5, +2 levels = 2.5)
